utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Again may I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, on behalf of the Prosecution it's Joanna Korner, Alexis Demirdjian, and case manager Jasmina Bosnjakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Appearing for Stanisic Defence, Slobodan Zecevic and Slobodan Cvijetic on my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, for Zupljanin, Igor Pantelic; Dragan Krgovic, co-counsel; Mr. Brent Hicks, legal assistant attorney-at-law from Florida; and Mr. Eric Tully, our case manager. Thank you. As well as our client here as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we formally begin this morning's session, I would wish on behalf of the Chamber and indeed on behalf of counsel and the parties, to thank the interpreters for the -- their indulgence yesterday. We appreciate that the events of yesterday would have put a fair amount of pressure on them, and we are grateful to them for accommodating us. Thank you. Mr. Zecevic, we are given to understand that there are a number of procedural matters that you wish to raise this morning before we resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, but there are two really urgent matters which I think I should address right now. And the rest of the matters we can -- we can deal with that in the course of the day whenever it pleases the Court. It's a number of substantial matters, and I can discuss with my colleague Ms. Joanna Korner and we agree that this should be brought to the attention of the Trial Chamber. Now, let me -- let me start very quickly with the two matters which I -- which I wanted to raise this morning. The first is yesterday decision on protective measures is a matter of concern for the Defence. Namely, so far in this case, apart from expert Robert Donia, all other witnesses have been under protective measures, which is out of five witnesses, four have been under protective measures. This is clearly in contrast to the right of the public and fair trial which is guaranteed to our clients by the statute. In this case, in this case of the coming witness, I believe despite the comment that I made, and His Honour Judge Harhoff agreed with that comment, the question was never asked. The question being why the witness in -- by his own wish withdraw -- ask that the protective measures for him will be withdrawn in the Karadzic case. And I checked and I see that the decision of the Karadzic Chamber is still standing. So therefore, despite the fact that he might not be called in the Karadzic case as a witness, the decision on his protective measures still stands, and I believe it is only right that the witness should be asked that question why did he ask in the other case that the protective measures be withdrawn in light of what he explained his concerns to us yesterday. So it is -- it is the position of the Defence that we would like the Trial Chamber to reconsider that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I seem to recall that in the course of the submissions yesterday that apart from the fact of the witness no longer being in the Karadzic case, the distinction that was apparent was the, A, perhaps tenuous but nevertheless an existing connection with Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, please, while we discuss this because I think it is going to discuss matters which will disclose his identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Korner. Yes, so we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the second matter is -- of concern is the ruling of yesterday. We believe that the rules of conduct or the guidelines have been altered as was set by the Trial Chamber. Now, the situation as we understood yesterday's ruling is that the Defence is expected to notify on the length of cross-examination of the witness not less than 24 hours in advance. But that creates two problems. The problem number one is we have no prior notice what exhibits the calling party will use with the witness. It is not in the pre-trial brief and nowhere else, as far as I can gather. On top, it's contrary to the procedural guidelines which you -- which you gave us, the guideline part 11 and part 12. The guideline 11 says that the rule is 72 hours before if it's over a hundred pages, and 48 hours if it's less than a hundred pages. And the procedural guideline number 12, it says that the final list, the calling party -- I will read: "The calling party shall submit the final list of documents or material to be used during examination-in-chief no later than 4.00 p.m. on the working day prior to the testimony of the witness." Before we get this information and be able to -- to assess that information, we cannot give you, obviously, and I hope you understand that it is impossible for the Defence to give an estimation of the length of the cross-examination before this particular data is known to the Defence. That is -- that is, in essence, my second submission, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, we just discussed that before, so Zupljanin Defence is also on the same line with the submission of my colleague Zecevic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel. It's a matter that the Chamber will continue to consider. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. Can I just say, I'm not able to see -- Mr. Zecevic did discuss this with me last night, and of course we will help out as much as we can. We've given him the 65 ter documents that are going to be used with the witness on Monday already. But for the life of me I can't see how which documents are going to be used affects their ability to tell us how long they're going to be in cross-examination. We will tell them how long we are going to be in examination-in-chief, and then they know what they want to cross-examine on presumably, and therefore our documents -- for the life of me, I can't see that, and I explained that to Mr. Zecevic last night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: For the information of those persons -- for the information of those persons seated in the gallery, the blinds are only being lowered to allow a witness who has certain protective measures to enter the courtroom. They will be raised as soon as he has taken his seat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting for the witness, we've printed out the list of abbreviations relating to the police. I hope Your Honours have got a copy. It was attached to the pre-trial brief. Well, they're here. Can we hand them up now so at least Your Honours have them in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you were sworn in yesterday, and I remind you you're still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to start by asking you to look at a piece of paper, please. You will see on there there's a number, ST-27, and underneath can you confirm that that's your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As you were told yesterday by Their Honours, you will be known purely by the witness number. Perhaps you'd just like to sign, though, to confirm that's your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, in order to establish this witness's background, may I ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you a little bit -- not a lot, but how the police operated, as I said, in pre-conflict Bosnia. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: First of all, is this correct: That there was, as it were, a hierarchy of police for better -- want of a better word, police stations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you just briefly explain to Their Honours how that hierarchy worked from the top downwards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a Republican Secretariat for the Interior at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Just below that were the various centres, security services, the CSBs, below which there was a certain number of police stations or public security stations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was there anything lower than a public security station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certain public security stations had their departments or branches.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did the -- I think in pre-war -- pre-conflict Bosnia there were some nine CSBs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall what the exact number was, but more or less each larger town in Bosnia-Herzegovina had a CSB seat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell us now about the reporting system? How did that work? Who reported to whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Public security stations were answerable to the CSBs, and the CSBs, in turn, reported to the ministry or the then-Republican secretariat of the interior in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How would the reporting take place? In other words, by what mechanisms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By virtue of meetings, collegiums, in writing, by phone, by facsimile [Realtime transcript read in error "e-mail"]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In your police station, and as I say, don't tell us where that was, how would reports be sent to the CSB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By official mail, and some things were arranged over the phone or by facsimile.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Firstly, how often would the report have to be made to the CSB in writing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it happened every three months, semi-annually and annually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So those were reports of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the situation concerning security in the respective areas of police stations, then the traffic issues, crime issues, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So that was really, what, a survey of what happened over the previous three months or whatever it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So what would be reported a daily -- well, firstly, was there daily reporting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when there were important events. In such cases each public security station was duty-bound to report such events to their CSBs, even on a daily basis if needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what sort of -- can you just give us an example of a daily event that might have to be reported? I'm sorry, an important event.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, say if a serious crime had taken place, then it would be reported to the CSB, and they then decided whether they would engage their own forces or provide certain equipment that they had at their disposal which was absent in the various police stations and which might help in shedding light on that particular crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was discipline like in the police then? In other words, was it strongly enforced or was it fairly relaxed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was strongly enforced.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If the head of the SJB received an order from the chief of the CSB, what would happen if he didn't obey that order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would probably suspended and disciplinary proceedings would be initiated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us there were meetings that were held. How often were those meetings held? Were they regular, or were they only for special things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the regular security meetings for the respective CSBs would follow after each of the reports that would be sent, quarterly, semi-annually, or annually, or whenever the CSB or their heads deemed it necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And one final thing on this reporting of serious crime and the like. Were there any consequences if there was a failure to report a serious crime that had taken place in -- in the area in which you were working?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what were those consequences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Disciplinary liability.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If a police officer committed a crime himself, what would happen to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would be processed much as any other citizen would. The service would do its part of the work.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In pre-conflict Bosnia, did you ever come across a situation where a police officer who committed a crime was not actually arrested and processed and prosecuted but was sent into -- to the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you a little bit about the appointment of chiefs. First of all, of the CSBs. Who appointed the chief of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The republican secretary, that is to say the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then the chief of the SJB. Who appointed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same. It all came from the ministry, from Sarajevo. At that time it was called the republican secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to move to after the 1990 elections, when the three nationalist parties effectively won the seats in the Assembly. Did that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry. For the sake of clarity, I think my learned friend should ask witness what is his opinion about the determination of the nature of the parties, whether they're national, nationalist, or ordinary party, because this particular word "nationalist party" might be of importance for the case which goes in the another area. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I would have thought this would be a matter for cross-examination. It's for the Prosecution how to lead the evidence on which he wishes to rely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, my intervention was to simply in order to limit the time, not to waste too much time of the Trial Chamber, you know, to speed up things. But I will clarify that in cross-examination. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't want to interrupt my colleague, but have an intervention in the in the transcript. Page 18, line 17, it says e-mail, but I'm sure the witness says "telefax" or "telex" because e-mail didn't exist at the time. Thank you. That's 18, line 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sure that's right, Mr. Zecevic. Thank you. [Indiscernible] Mr. Pantelic. I didn't think there was any dispute that the three parties who won were nationalist.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. After the 1990 elections, what effect, if any, did that have on how heads of police stations, SJBs, let's stick to for the moment, were appointed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very outset, nothing changed. But later on, unfortunately, things worsened and people were being replaced because they were not of, how should I put it? Appropriate ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before 1990, did the appointments have anything to do with the ethnicity? In other words, was there a division between the three nationalities -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the so-called ethnic key was used so as to have equal representation of the three ethnic communities, although I don't think that was the decisive factor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that after the elections people were being replaced because they weren't of appropriate ethnicity. Can we stick to your police station. How was the ethnic -- what was the ethnic divide there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the SJB was a Muslim. The chief was a Serb, and I was assistant as a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did the -- in the appointment of -- of the chiefs, did the local political parties have any say in who was appointing who -- who was appointed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They usually approved the proposals.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could they make the appointments themselves or did those appointments have to be made by the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing could happen without the knowledge of the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we now move, please, to -- you've talked about -- began to talk about the changes that happened. How did those changes manifest themselves after the election in your particular police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the public security station was removed from duty, and for a while I was acting commander of the public security station in his place, and then the chief called me at one occasion and told me (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we just for safety's sake go into private session for the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You told us -- we're back so that the public can hear you, sir. You told us that the chief of the public security station replaced the head of the public security -- commander. That would be the commander. But what ethnicity was the man who had been replaced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, did you remain at this police station where you told us there was already this removal going on, or did you move?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I took over the duties of commander. This is what the chief told me. And this went on for two or three months.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us earlier whilst we were in private session that you -- in March of 1992 you moved to another police station. Can you tell us why you did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already mentioned it. Sometime in March 1992, the chief of the SJB called me to his office and told me he couldn't guarantee my security and that I should leave the station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And your move was to a station in a different municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't move to a different station. I was without a job for a while, and then representatives of the HDZ political party came and they offered me a post in the municipal secretariat in the municipality. I said that I was looking for a lasting solution in Croatia, but that in the meantime I would help them as much as I could.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, can I ask you whether there were any signs that the -- there were changes coming about in -- in the police station? For example, in uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard from colleagues who had remained at work, because in the meantime I had left the organisation. They had to change their uniforms, the insignia. Instead of the five-pointed star, they had to place the Serbian tricolour flag.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what about the writing on the uniforms? Did that change at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had to wear some sort of insignia. I don't remember it was on the left or the right shoulder, but perhaps it was on both shoulders. It was sign "Milicija" in the Cyrillic script.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what had it been before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier it was the same word, "Milicija," but it was in the Latin script.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And this is what you were told by someone who had remained in the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I also saw that on the streets.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you were offered your next post, as you've told us, did you start work in the police station there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the police station but at the Municipal Secretariat for National Defence, but the seat of the secretariat was in the same building where the police station was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can you just briefly explain what the Secretariat for National Defence did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those jobs are still not quite clear to me. I didn't have enough time to actually really get into the intricacies of it, but they dealt with military issues, mobilisation tasks. The alerting centre was part of the secretariat, co-operation with the military districts and administrative tasks, civilian protection, and it also closely co-operated with the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And again I apologise, I should have asked you this before: Apart from regular police was there also a reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a reserve police force which could be used as per need.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who would become police reservists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Citizens who were not in the regular police force but were part of the defence organisation and were assigned to the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence, was that again people who had done their JNA service and who were then reservists, as it were, for the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence is a separate structural unit which had a certain number of people who were there as professionals and then they would engage the reserve military forces as part of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Can I just again quickly for the next question go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whilst you were working for the Secretary Of National Defence, was there any kind of military presence in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How active at this stage, let's say, around March of 1992, April 1992, was that military presence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not active in that area. They were just present. The reserve force was engaged, and they were assigned to -- or deployed to several locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there any kind of mobilisation that took place at that stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a mobilisation which was carried out without my knowledge, because the Banja Luka Military District usurped the mobilisation sector which should have been working within the secretariat. But this was done without my knowledge, so I did lodge a protest with some people at the military district but without any results.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When the mobilisation, which was carried out without your knowledge, took place, who was mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone was mobilised. I don't know if it was the entire reserve force, but if you're thinking about ethnic classification, they were all mobilised. Some -- actually a major part of the Croat and Muslim population refused to respond to the mobilisation call-up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can I next ask you about weapons. In your municipality, were there weapons kept for the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Where were the weapons kept? I suppose, actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before it goes out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At this period, and if you can be careful, sir, about not mentioning, I know it's difficult, not mentioning the name of the municipality, were you aware of any arms being acquired by private citizens?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware personally, but there were stories going around that some individuals were obtaining arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. When you say some individuals, of what -- any particular ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All three ethnicities were mentioned, but from the things that reached me, it seems that weapons were bought from Serbs by Muslims and Croats. I don't know what quantities were involved though.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You say that weapons were bought from Serbs by Muslims and Croats. Why from Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the only ones at the time who had weapons and the possibility to obtain them in an illegal manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what was that? Why were the only ones who had weapons and the possibility to obtain them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons, the military weapons, were monitored by the Serb forces, and that's how they obtain them. I don't know if this was with somebody's knowledge or they were stealing them. In any case, they were reselling them, and this is how it was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you become aware of the events - and I'm moving now to April and May - that were taking place elsewhere in neighbouring municipalities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there was some military movements under way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you become aware of the changes -- well, let's -- I don't think there can be any dispute about this. Did you become aware of the declaration of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I found out from the media. You could hear about it on the radio, television.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And I'm going -- I'm going to ask you -- I'll go back and -- I'm sorry, we have to go back to private session for the actual names, but I wanted to ask you about some meetings you had with a military commander. Did you have meetings around this period, in May, with a military commander?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the witness comes back into court, can I just mention that we've received a medical report for Witness ST-203. It's been instantly translated, but I've had it read by our acting interpreter, case manager, it does say he's not fit to travel. We'll hand it in at the next break. We've also taken the opportunity at this break to discuss timings of witnesses, and it would seem on the timings of the witnesses arranged for next week, we would be asking for the videolink on Tuesday week, not Monday, as originally. And we're simply giving you advanced notification so that if you'd be kind enough at the end of today's proceedings to make a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Tuesday week would put you within the time that -- for required notice that the rules require?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, it won't, but we're hoping that you can -- it's not within ten days. Today is Friday. It would just, just about make it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, Mr. Pantelic, do you have a view on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we don't have any problem with -- with that if the -- if the witness appears on the -- on Tuesday via videolink, none whatsoever. We discussed with Ms. Korner already during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm this submission, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we would rule on that this afternoon. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then the witness can come back. I've indicated, sorry, to both my learned friends that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've indicated to my learned friends that I hope to finish this witness within the next hour, thereby, I hope, saving one hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we go into private session again for two or three questions and then we can go back into open.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've told us you were on your way to work on this day. What actually happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was stopped in the place I just mentioned by some uniformed personnel. I don't know whether it was the regular or reserve force of the military. In any case, they wore camouflage uniforms. They asked for my ID. They asked me for weapons. I told them I didn't have any. One of them seems to have (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause there for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. Can we have that redacted, please. Line 7 and 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, the -- the building that they took you to, and don't mention the name of it, what sort of a building was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a building belonging to a company. I suppose they had their offices there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this building that they took you to, was anybody else there in the building, or was it just you on your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone. I don't know whether there was anyone else in the building. In any case, I was alone in the room.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how long were you kept there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 6.30 or 7.00 a.m. and 4.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Were there guards there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able -- you -- you told us the people who stopped you wore camouflage uniforms. Are you able to say what kind of uniforms they were? In other words, police or military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military olive-drab uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did any of the guards say anything to you whilst you were there about what was happening elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one told me anything. When I asked that I be allowed to go into the town to help alleviate the situation if anything strange was going on, then one of them told me to lie low because it was better for me to do so since there was something going on in town which was not good and it would not have been good for me to be there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you told us you were kept there till 4.00 in the afternoon --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, we do need to go into private session for the following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, sir, people cannot hear what you're saying so --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just is second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. We reached the stage where you had been transferred from the building where you were first taken to after you'd been stopped, and you're now in a building elsewhere, and you've explained how you were against the wall, people passing were beaten -- beating you. How long were you kept against the wall?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: (redacted). We just spoke briefly there, and then he ordered those people there not to touch me and that I didn't have to be against the wall anymore and that I had to stay there for the interview. And I said I didn't know why I was there. There's nothing particular, no reason. So I did have to stay there, and then he said I would be released.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that's all right. I'm not going to ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The person who spoke to you, was they the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you were kept there for about an hour, and what happened to you after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that I just stood there without having to lean on the wall. I stood in one place. I was not allowed to move. If I just happened to bend down or my knees bent a little bit, I would receive a blow or something like that. And I spent about an hour there. It was perhaps 10.00 or 11.00 at night when I was taken to an office - I don't recall

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we better just, I'm sorry, for safety's sake, just for a minute, go into private session. And could that be redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, sir, the public can now hear you. So you said that a man approached you whom you knew whilst you were standing in this corridor. What did he do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the police force. We went to the police academy together. I think he had the rank of inspector. I don't know exactly what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When he approached you, what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We greeted each other. He asked me what I was doing there. I said I didn't know. I had no idea that I was brought there. He said all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I stop you there. We'd moved on from that. You told us that this man came up to you, not who you were at school with but later after that, somebody you also knew. Did he give you anything, the second man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another man came up to me, but that was when I was taken upstairs to one of the officers -- offices. I also knew this man from before. He gave me some sort of paper with the explanation that it's night, it's late, they will continue tomorrow, but I should sign this paper. And from what I was able to read quickly then, it was saying that I had been arrested and that I was being charged for some sort of armed insurgency. I refused to sign the paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Had you taken part in any kind of armed insurgency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you refused to sign the piece of paper. Were you further questioned that day or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was taken to prison after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. The following day were you brought back to that building from the prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And before you were brought back and whilst you were at the prison, did anything happen to you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I was placed in the prison. Up until the time that I reached the prison I was standing in the corridor, and I received I don't know how many blows all over my body. Once I came to the prison, before I was put into a cell I was beaten just like the other two persons who came with me, and I was taken to solitary confinement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And were the other two persons who came with you those who you mentioned had been in the van at the time of the arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How were you beaten before you were put into a cell? With what, and ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were beaten by fists. We were kicked. We were hit with bats. And then when I was taken to solitary confinement, then this one person there continued to punch me and kick me. He hit me a couple of times with his pistol, but at one point he pushed the pistol into my mouth. He damaged one of my teeth. I still have the marks of that. He threatened that he would kill me with a knife. It's some sort of knife which I understood had been seized, and it was used to kill somebody. And then he would pass judgement on me. I mean, in that atmosphere of fear I wasn't really paying attention. I tried to block the force of the blows by standing to one side or the other. I tried to evade the blows.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was it just this one person there, or were there more people there while this was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was alone. While I was in the solitary confinement. When we were beaten, we were together in the prison corridor. Then there were several of them who were beating not only me but the other two people as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You told us you were taken back the next day to the building where you'd been standing against the wall. What happened to you during that time when you were back at the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken to one of the offices. I was approached by a person who introduced himself as an inspector. The conversation began on the topic of some weapons, obtaining weapons. Since I had no idea about this and I didn't take part in any kind of weapon procurement or any kind of organisation, the conversation went round in circles a few times. Things were repeated. Then the person went to another room. He returned. I don't remember if it was on the same day or the next day when I was brought in again. He told me that he didn't know why I was there, that he would prefer to release me, which I did ask for, but then I was told that there was some kind of Crisis Staff in the area of the municipality where I was arrested, and this Crisis Staff wouldn't permit something like that to happen. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's what the person who was interrogating you told you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If you just very carefully listen to the question. Did you know -- had you -- sorry. Frame the question properly. Was this person interrogating you someone you had met before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able to find out, though, of what nationality he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He told me his first and last name. He told me that he was allegedly a Croat. I don't know if he was or not, if he gave me his correct name. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you told us -- you said a moment ago that you don't remember whether it was on the same day or the next day. How many days were you taken back and forth to this building where you were questioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this went on for five or six days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The other two people who you had been arrested with in the sense of you were together, were they also being taken back and forth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you interrogated together or separately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Separately.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there any repetition of what had happened to you that first night at the prison, in other words, the beatings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beating wasn't like that, but I really couldn't say exactly. A lot of time has passed since then. I don't remember if there was any beating after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any injuries as a result of -- of the beating you received? Apart from your tooth, any other injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other than bruises and the haematoma, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you given any kind of medical treatment for the injury to your tooth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whilst you were at the prison, could you hear what was happening in other cells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in solitary confinement I heard screams, moans. Evidently people were getting beaten there. I don't know who was doing the beating and who was getting beaten, I wasn't there, but other prisoners talked about this later when I was transferred to a cell where there were more prisoners who were there serving their sentence. I guess the civilians who had committed certain crimes had already been there. They had nothing to do with the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How long a period did you remain in that prison being taken for interrogation? You said you went back five or six days for questioning. Did you stay in the prison longer than the questioning those four or five days, or after those four or five days were you moved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After those few days that we spent in the prison, after the interrogations were finished, we were transferred to the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay, just --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just for one moment can we go into private session, and you tell us where that was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry about this, Your Honour. I know it's irritating, but it's one of the problems.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We're back in public again, sir. So you were taken to this elementary school with the other people that you mentioned, and you said you were taken to a bathroom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How big roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a couple of showers there, water taps. I don't know. Perhaps it was 3 X 4 or 4 X 4. It was a room of some 10 to 12 square metres. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were the three of you kept together, or were you separated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed together.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you when you got to that bathroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we entered the bathroom, these so-called Specials had formed a gauntlet which we had to pass through where we did receive a substantial beating.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's deal with the Specials, as you call them. What do you mean by Specials?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are special units set up at that time. They were call Specijalci, and since I'm from the same profession I can say they were far from being Specials. That was just a group of savages.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You say you were from the same profession. Does that mean these were police officers, allegedly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were special units of theirs, and they were wearing camouflage uniforms of predominantly dark and light blue colours rather than olive-drab colours. It was that combination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know where the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Korner, what's -- Mr. Witness, what is the significance of the colour? You mentioned that the camouflage uniforms that these men were wearing were blueish somehow, with mixed blue colours, and that was different from the green and brown camouflage uniforms. Now, the significance of the blue colour in these camouflage uniform, was that that these people in the gauntlets were employed with the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They were engaged by the police. I don't know if these were regular or reserve forces, because they were set up as some sort of separate unit, and they wore this uniform to differentiate themselves from the army. The army wore olive-drab uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Other than their uniforms, was there anything else to indicate that they were some kind of police officers? Were they -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were they carrying anything which indicated that they were police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had their sidearms. They had handcuffs, long-barrelled weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've told us that you knew about these so-called Specials. Had you seen the Special Police before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you say "Like that, no," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see that type of uniform before, and also I'm not going to comment on their conduct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Well, that's -- leaving aside their conduct, if you hadn't seen that sort of uniform before, how did you know it was a police uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were there the whole time and in the course of the conversation, we understood that these were some sort of special units that had nothing to do with the regular police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So this is what you learnt from them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is how they addressed one another and talked amongst one another, and you could conclude that these were some sort of special units. I'm not sure whether they were composed from the regular police forces. I kind of doubt that, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen any parade involving men wearing this colour of uniform? On television news or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot be certain. It's possible that I did see them. I think that I did see them on television, but that was the first time that I had actually seen them for real.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, let's go back to, as you've described it, the gauntlet. Can I ask you to give us a little more detail about what actually happened to you and your -- the other two men. What did they do to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were passing through the gauntlet we were punched, kicked, hit by rifle butts, bats. We were beaten until we reached the bathroom. Once we entered the bathroom they continued to beat us, and then they left us alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you -- it may be obvious, but did you recognise any of the people there. Just answer it yes or not, because if it's yes, we'll have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, how long were you kept in the -- that elementary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 10 to 15 days. I don't know the exact length of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: During those 10 to 15 days were you beaten again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you suffer injuries as a result of those beatings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During one of the beatings I lost my consciousness. I fainted from the blows. I didn't break anything, but I had bruises all over my body.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about food and water? Were you given those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did receive minimal amounts. One of the local -- locals, a Serb who evidently disagreed with this whole stupidity that was going on and probably knowing -- I assume that he knew one of the two people who were there detained with me, because he couldn't have known me because I had left that area a long time ago, he would sneak in food for us that he would leave on the window, cigarettes, plum brandy, things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you said that you were beaten while you were still held in this building several times. And my question is just, were it the same group of people in blue camouflage uniforms that did the beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't really say because I didn't know any of the people who were there. They could have been the same people or different people. I don't know exactly who these people were individually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No. Thank you, but how were they dressed? Were they also wearing blue camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there anybody else forming part of these people who were beating you who were wearing other kinds of uniforms, or was it always the blue camouflage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They always wore the blue camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, again can you just answer this yes or no: Whilst you were at the school, did some people come to the school whom you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, private session for just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you told us that you received visitors, and you've explained what they did whilst you were at this elementary school. Can you tell us how long altogether did you remain at the elementary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 10 and 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then were you taken back to the prison in the town that you've originally told us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were taken back to the civilian prison where we spent some four or four and a half months.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And from there were you transferred to another prison, as you've told us, which was in fact a military prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, during the course of this imprisonment, were you charged with any kind of offence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion I was taken to either a court or a military prosecutor's office where an indictment against me was read out. It said something to the extent that I was being charged with the commission of the crime of organising an armed rebellion against illegally elected authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Leaving aside the legality of the authorities, had you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 61, line 17, against the legally elected authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He said legally elected authorities, and that's what he confirmed just now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's right. I heard him say that as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Had you -- had you organised any kind of armed rebellion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've told us you were taken to a court or a military prosecutor's office. Did you ever have a trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that one occasion when I was taken there, the indictment was shown to me. I provided a statement. My attorney, who was appointed ex officio, was present as well, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you ever discover the name of the person who was showing the indictment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He introduced himself, and later on I received a document with his name on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Are you able to remember the name now, or would you need to see the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can say his name. May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think there's any problem if you'd like to say his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Svetozar Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you ever told that you'd been convicted or were being sentenced or anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Quite the contrary. On one occasion I received a decision of sorts which said that the military prosecutor's office conducted an investigation and failed to establish the existence of any elements of the crime that I was being charged with and that I should be released. There was quite a fascinating legal remedy towards the end of the document which read that the party, the accused party has no right to appeal the decision given that the party had waived that right, whatever that meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Had you waived any rights that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the day of exchange, it was then that I received that piece of paper. I was forced to sign a sheet of paper, an A4 paper, which was blank. I signed it, and I have no idea what they subsequently put on that sheet of paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Before we come to your exchange, you've told us you were taken to a military prison. How long were you kept there for? Roughly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe a month or a few days more or less than that. I don't know precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was your treatment like in that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the transfer from the civilian to the military prison, all three of us received gruesome beating by the military and the judiciary police. We were beaten in the civilian as well as in the military prison. In the military prison, after that, we were beaten on a few other occasions in the room where we were accommodated. After I was taken to see the military prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: After the beatings, I was taken to the military prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... And I complained to him. The prosecutor said that this was not to have happened, and that he should see -- he will see to it. At that time I just thought they were playing the good cop/bad cop game with me, but indeed a colonel arrived later with a Serbian accent and apologised for what had happened. And indeed in the 20-some days after that while I was still in the camp no one touched me. They even provided some newspapers and books.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you and the two other people that you've throughout who were effectively arrested the same day and together, did you remain together throughout the period of your incarceration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were separated in the civilian prison as well as in the military prison for a while, although a certain portion of the time spent in the military prison we did spend together.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whilst you were in the two prisons, the civilian and military, were there other people that you knew being brought in as prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know those people. With time I learned of a person's name who was also detained there in one of the cells, but that is all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What I'm trying to get at is the people who were being brought in, of what nationality were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Firstly and -- first and foremost it was Muslims and Croats. While we were in the civilian prison, some people were brought into my cell in different periods. To be precise, there were three Serbs who were brought in. One was from the area of Gradiska, Bosanska Gradiska. Allegedly he was charged with selling weapons to the Muslims. There was another one who was brought in from Prijedor because allegedly he had killed another Serb. And a third came in from Bosanski Novi. He may have been a part of a group which had committed certain crimes, and then they were brought in.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know crimes against whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In discussion with that person, because we talked in the cell, he boasted of killing Muslims and Croats. I don't know whether that was true or whether he was just boasting. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And finally, sir, you've told us you were exchanged. Do you know when you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So from the 11th of June until the 28th of November you were in custody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Those are the questions I ask. Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As you commence your cross-examination, you will bear in mind that we are scheduled for a break in about five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Witness. My name is Slobodan Cvijetic. I'm an attorney-at-law, and I'm a co-counsel for Mr. Mico Stanisic. In this introductory portion, I wanted to deal with certain answers you gave to the Prosecutor. In my cross-examination, I have to deal with what you have testified to during your testimony. One question to start with: In the tripartite division of power and parliamentary systems where we have the legislative, judicial, executive branches, you will agree with me that the police belongs to the executive branch? Do you agree with me? You have to utter a spoken answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the police is part of the state administration, the state apparatus providing for the functioning of that state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In order for such a state organ to function, certain state administration regulations apply.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Among others, this includes the law on state administration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Law on the general administrative procedure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: By way of example, if a citizen turns to the CSB or a police station or the ministry with a request, without going into the different types of requests such as changing place of residence, issuing a new ID, and so on and so forth, that is decided within --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, it's very good that you are able to speak the same language as the witness so that you can communicate freely, but the interpreters have to be able to follow you, and unless we are able to understand what you're saying, then this is all for no good reason. So please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've already been cautioned twice by my learned colleague Mr. Zecevic for the very same reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that in the hierarchy of managing and supervising a state body, the minister of interior or the minister of defence, since you were defence secretary, manages and supervises such a state organ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You've already answered to Ms. Korner that if a policeman or any other official of the Ministry of the Interior and the police committed an offence contrary to his orders and duties, that person is then included in any disciplinary proceedings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Does the same apply to all other employees of all other state administration bodies, for example, the Secretariat of National Defence, the Registrar's Office in a municipality, et cetera? Does the same type of procedure apply if they do not follow the duties and tasks assigned to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Another thing that Ms. Korner asked you. You mentioned the issue of reporting. You spoke of the line of reporting within the Ministry of the Interior. Perhaps we can just offer some further clarification. Was reporting done per departments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe you have cautioned me of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Korner, may I ask you, you mentioned at the last session that some documents that you wanted to put to the witness were not included in your 65 ter list, so we MFI'd them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: My question is, yet, they seem to have a 65 ter number. How come -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I asked the case manager the same thing. I think they're just allocated a number as far as I understand it. Because I was going to simply refer to the ERN numbers, but they don't become exhibits. Is that -- yeah. They're just given -- if any documents are going to be referred to, despite the fact that they're not on our 65 ter list, they are just given a number which is not really a 65 ter number. It just a -- it is an identification number, but we're just following through. So, I mean, that's the best I can do. I'm not altogether clear myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So the 65 ter number is not a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not a real 65 ter number. It's an imaginary 65 ter number. Can I put it that way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very inventive. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just mention. I'm told there is no prospect of this witness finishing today. I gather the Stanisic team is going to take up the rest of the time. I forgot to tell him, I wonder if Your Honours would be kind enough, that he will have to stay over the weekend, but he cannot speak to any members of the OTP. I just forgot to mention that myself. Or anybody, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, we stopped as we were talking about reporting along the line the of the work, so could you please explain these line of work or, as we call them, their departments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean within the police, the Ministry of Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes. We're talking about the MUP the whole time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the MUP was at the top with a seat in Sarajevo. Then you had the security services centres, and below them were the public security stations. So each CSB had a number of SJBs. I don't know how many, depends on the structure of the MUP how they did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And in that organisation as you presented it to us, were there any departments and those lines of work? I'm trying to help you. Was there a police department, public security department, traffic department, criminal investigations, and did they have their own lines of work? This is the kind of thing that I was thinking of.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was sectors, sections within the ministry, and you had similar things within the public security centres, and the public security stations themselves had criminal investigations units, traffic, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you that precisely. Did this -- each of those lines report up along its own line of reporting, ending at the assistant or deputy minister in charge of that department? For example, the criminal investigation units, they had their own line of reporting. This is what I was thinking of. Is it correct what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it should have functioned. I don't know if it actually did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My colleague Mr. Zecevic has drawn my attention to the fact that because my speed, a question was missed out and even an answer. I'm going to repeat that, and of course I expect the same answer. I actually asked you if, conditionally speaking, the police, because when I say the police I'm thinking about the whole MUP, so if the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the centre and the police station is addressed by a citizen with a request to have a passport issued, ID card, report to a place of residence, or sign out of a particular place of residence, the decision on that request was made on the basis of the rules of general administrative proceedings, a certificate would be issued to him which he would have the right to appeal, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That part is not there. So let us go back now. I'm now going to back to the top of the ministry that you were dealing with. At one point during your testimony you said, and there's no reason for us not to confirm that there after multi-party elections, the Minister of Internal Affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina was Alija Delimustafic, is that correct, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The minister of defence Jerko Doko was a Croat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I was asking you because -- not really because of their ethnicity, but they were both civilians, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And they ran their organs as organs of administration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: For purposes of administration and management, they adopted general regulations dealing with organisational personnel and other matters so that their organs would function within the system of state administration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that the Ministry of Internal Affairs is specific in that it has its uniformed part, it has persons with special authority. They don't necessarily have to wear uniforms, but these can be inspectors with special powers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And these special powers - I'm not going to enumerate them - comprise, for example, that in certain situations they can apply force, they can deprive certain citizens of freedom or -- these powers are derived on the basis of the law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And that special law that is applied in the MUP is the Law on Internal Affairs, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So can I conclude, and I think that you would agree with me, that when - and you were an inspector yourself - when a policeman is supposed to detain or arrest somebody for committing a crime or for being suspected of committing a crime, they arrest that person on the basis of the law and the powers that are entrusted to them according to the law.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And they are obliged to say that they are arresting them in the name of the law, and they are obliged also to inform them of their rights that they have under the law.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that there is no order required for this procedure from the MUP because they are an official with these powers granted to them under the law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: A remark to the transcript, so he does not need an order from the minister and not the ministry. I hope the witness understood. I would just like to have this corrected in the transcript. And now that we're talking about officials with powers, sir, in response to a question by the Prosecutor, What is your rank, you replied that you were an inspector. I'm going to try to clarify that. Is inspector a title? I think that it is. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to correct that for the purposes of the transcript. Can we call that a functional designation? I think that that is how it's described.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to move to another topic, sir. In response to questions by Madam Prosecutor Ms. Korner, she dealt with that a little bit, but I would like to go into further detail. We're talking about appointments at the Ministry of Internal Affairs. You spoke about a regular procedure of appointment within the MUP, and if it's not a problem for you, if you can just briefly remind us how, according to the law, these appointments should be effected.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All appointments would be subject to agreement of the MUP headquarters in Sarajevo regardless of whether we're talking about a policeman at the time in the SJB or a chief. The difference is in that when we're talking about management posts --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm going to ask you about that later, so don't rush ahead. So I have received an answer from you that I was interested in. I would just like to digress slightly. The Ministry of Internal Affairs employs administrative personnel as well as policemen and authorised officials. Can you please tell me how one would become an employee of the MUP, regardless of at what level, in the administrative section?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would be a vacancy announced. If these were some special posts perhaps no vacancy would need to be announced. The candidates would pass some tests, and that would be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And how would a person become a uniformed policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was working there, a vacancy would be announced for admissions to the police high school or secondary school. Certain tests, physical and aptitude tests would be conducted, and then there would be a selection process, and those who were accepted to the high school would eventually become policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. All right. Now we have clarified the regular legal procedure. But you would agree with me, would you not, that following the multi-party elections there was some changes, and that meant that politics began to interfere in appointments at the MUP. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that I'm to call them the winning parties, I'm not going to -- so I'm talking about the SDA, the SDS, and the HDZ, among other things, showed a certain interest for specific posts within the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
