utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: After the multi-party elections, these personnel combinations began to occur. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The parties began to push forward their own people into the MUP -- or within the MUP at practically all levels; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Was this policy so far advanced that they -- that even affected the reserve police forces in order for the parties to find a place for as many as possible of their supporters in different positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, in this way wasn't there a danger that the Ministry of Internal Affairs would have employed people who, according to the regular procedure, would not meet the requirements for employment at the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Would it be possible for the reserve police forces in this way to accommodate many individuals who did not meet even the elementary requirements to become policemen? Perhaps some of them even had criminal records or were previously prosecuted. Did you have information about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have specific information, but there was such a possibility as the number of these people suddenly increased.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that the number of the reserve police force suddenly expanded, and you allow for the possibility that among the people who became members were people who had criminal records and such.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, pursuant to the law, would it be up to the Minister of Internal Affairs to order that such persons be removed from the reserve police forces? Would that be something that would be in accordance to the law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would think so, yes, in adhering to the proper procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: If we're talking about the imminent danger of war, and we're talking about military conscripts according to their state of health and date of birth, perhaps it would be convenient to place them at the disposal of the military authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that situation, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can I just ask you a question to supplement the question by counsel. Do you know if any screening was made of the new police recruits of their criminal background? I mean, was it possible at the time to -- to ensure that new recruits to the reserve police force and to the police force did not have a criminal background? Was it -- my question is: Was it possible and, if so, was it done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was possible to check that if somebody wanted to do that, but I don't know if it was actually done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to continue since I know how long you were in the police. This policy of accepting such people, did it continue for as long as you remained in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For as long as I was in the police, no one was accepted in the regular forces, outside of the regular procedure, let me put it that way, but I think in the area where I was, that's all I can talk about, not the area where I had been detained but in the area where I worked in the police, up until the time before I left that area, no one was accepted into the ranks outside of the framework of the rules, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I was thinking more about the reserve forces. Do you have information about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to continue about the order to get rid of such people from the ranks of the police. If on the basis of legal procedure such persons were removed and placed at the disposal of the military, were they then practically exonerated from their criminal responsibility and not punished for what they had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did the MUP minister have the power to exonerate them? Not only them but any other citizen and allow them to evade the responsibility for what they had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't [Realtime transcript read in error "done"] think that he could have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me, and you also said yourself that if a policeman happened to commit some crime you would treat him just like any other citizen. You would prosecute him or allow the authorised prosecutorial bodies to deal with him. Does that also apply to the dismissed reserve policemen? Would they also be subject to the same procedure? Or if they had already been put through this procedure by the prosecutor and the courts, would the proceedings then continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In normal times, yes, that would be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interruption. Correction to transcript, please. Page 77, line 7. I think it should be clarified. Witness said I do not think. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, following the multi-party elections, you would agree with me, as you said, that politics began to interfere. And perhaps you would agree with my conclusion that in a way that is how the regular appointment system within the MUP was disrupted with this interference or meddling of politics.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a certain extent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to draw your attention to one more new thing that emerged on the political scene of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Crisis Staffs appeared, namely. How do you see them? How would you define them? I know what your testimony was in other cases, but I would like to hear you now say that. How do you define them, and how do you see -- view the fact that they started to appear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I just learned about the existence of these Crisis Staffs, I was already arrested. So I considered them as kind of staffs that would deal with certain matters at the level of the municipality within that structure, something like that. However, in the meantime I saw a piece of paper about some law being adopted. I don't know what it's called. Adopted in Republika Srpska or Republika Srpska Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I read that, and on the basis of what I read I came to the conclusion that this Crisis Staff was superior, and it was -- it ranked above the police itself, above police forces, which was anachronistic as far as I'm concerned. I don't know whoever adopted that, but what do I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that you identified -- you testified identically in a different case, and you used the exact same term, anachronistic. Would you say it was more a question of an abnormal situation? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, certainly. I don't see the reason for such a body to exist because this area was already regulated in the law on national defence, through the Territorial Defence, through the army, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So would you agree with me then that we have one more form of disruption of the whole system of decision-making, of control and management of the MUP through this existence of the Crisis Staffs? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the structure in this way of these Crisis Staffs and the way that was regulated, everything had become disrupted. The to-date system was disrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, there will be expert witnesses appearing here who will deal with Crisis Staffs, so we don't need to go into more detail about their -- the way they were formed and their ambit, but I would like to have your answers to a couple of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to see document 65 ter 690. Can we look at page 2, please. Second page, please. This is just the title page of the document. Thank you very much. And can the witness look at the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the document? Can you read it from the monitor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go into private session. This has come up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I prepared myself for this examination, cautioning myself on my notes that I shouldn't address this witness by his name but by his pseudonym. So I do have this in mind. Your Honours, I seek to tender the document I showed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, technically he can't do that because this witness was actually locked up at the time that this document was produced, and he can't do anything about it. However, if it helps, it's certainly a document that's going to come in through another witness. So whether it comes in now -- I'm not sure that -- are you trying to make it a Defence exhibit? Oh, all right. It's just going to complicate matters, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I explain, Your Honour? Your Honours, I'm discussing with the witness the impact or influence of Crisis Staffs on the work of police organs, and they're basically meddling with all the functions of the Ministry of the Interior. An example of this are the documents that I'm seeking to tender through this witness. Therefore, I believe this is sufficiently relevant for you to have it admitted. Otherwise, if I may add, we could have tendered this as our exhibit, but that would mean duplicating it with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: One of the things that we have difficulty appreciating is the nexus between this particular document and the witness. We appreciate -- pardon me. We appreciate what Ms. Korner says about this document coming in at a later stage, but can this witness properly speak to this document which was created -- which he didn't create and which was created at a time when - thanks - when he had no control over his personal circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have provided an explanation as to why I believe this to be a good example of our assertions concerning the behaviour of Crisis Staffs and their relations -- their relationship to the Ministry of Interior as confirmed by the witness. If you believe that this witness is not the best witness to tender his document through, I will do it with another witness, but if I may, I would just like to have the witness comment on this document without me tendering it. Do you agree with that proposal of mine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But to what end? Comment on it to what end?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To shed some light on this issue, to see whether the witness is denying or confirming some of the things we have been discussing in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I assist. This witness has told the Court that he doesn't know anything about Crisis Staffs except he was shown on a document in the last trial. This witness cannot comment at all on a document he hasn't seen, on a topic he doesn't know anything about. There are going to be many other witnesses, including the signatory to this document, who my learned friend can ask questions about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It seems to us that you have taken this witness as far as you can with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In principle, then, I will just ask the witness whether he has any information about the Crisis Staffs meddling with the affairs of the Ministry of Interior and to what extent.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't have such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that you read some documents from which you concluded that the Crisis Staffs basically became the principal organs deciding on everything possible, even in things which fell under the competence of the Ministry of the Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Not only the Ministry of the Interior but even national defence matters or All People's Defence matters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Hence you won't be surprised if say that they even decided on the appointments of certain police station commanders, about mobilisation and similar issues.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about the functioning of the Crisis Staffs. However, I have read the particular document, regulation on the remit of the Crisis Staffs, and based on that I conclude that this may well have been the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you also agree with me if I say that they even appointed -- or established certain police stations, not only their commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. That they established new police stations?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I have a document to that effect, but I'm not allowed to show it to you. But would you be surprised if you learned that they did things like that as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything is possible when a system breaks down.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then in principle, we can agree that this system, the police system, as well as the system of managing, supervising, and appointing was further undermined by the appearance of the Crisis Staffs? Am I correct in presuming that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: After having worked for the police, you began working in one of the organs tasked with national defence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And in a way, you are competent enough to answer several questions from that domain. Can you tell me, what is the system of command in the armed forces as you have been describing it in the previous cases? For example, the principle of singleness of command or unity of command, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I seem to recall having learned about it in the police high school, if that's the principle of singleness of command. In a state of imminent threat of war or a state of war, the police would be a component which under such circumstances fell under the armed forces system. This in turn means that the supreme commander was the then-Presidency of the SFRY, and the system existed all the way from the top down to the units at grass-root level. As for any further functioning of the system, I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't expect it from you. I just wanted to ask you about this pyramid, pyramid of decision-making and command in the armed forces. At the top of the pyramid, as you say, was the collective Presidency of the SFRY, but not as the Presidency but as the supreme commander of the armed forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned that this ensured that there is civilian control over the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Below the supreme commander there was the staff of the armed forces with its chief. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Further down the pyramid we have the various military units without going into the detail now. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The gist of my question is whether the pyramid could have two tops. We know of the Egyptian ones. They only have one. But what about this one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one, too, could only have one top. If there was another, that must have been a paramilitary top.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It seems you strike at the heart of my argument. The principle of singleness of command includes only one top. If there is another top the entire defence system caves in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: A question or two about the Ministry of the Interior next. What happens if the Supreme Command decides that some police forces be engaged in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was their right to do so under the then-constitution and laws, and indeed this could be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What is the statute -- the status of such police units and their commanders which are made part of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They enjoy the same status as other members of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree then that their separate police authority ceases to exist. They become members of the armed forces under the command of their commanders [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An intervention for the transcript. It should be their military commanders instead of commanders only. This is what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, when such police forces are included into the armed forces, that decision needs to be based by the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Needs to be made by the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The entire police structure, then, needs to adapt itself to the new situation, i.e., they need to implement that decision.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's an order. It needs to be followed through. No doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know what "resubordination" means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can suppose, I can venture a guess, but I hear it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Does the fact of subordinating police forces to the armed forces can be determined resubordination? Am I making myself clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, we come into the domain of the application of the law on All People's Defence. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please show 1D004042 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, while that's happening, can I just remind Your Honours that there should be time at the end. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Counsel, it is clear that we're not going to be able to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It is clear that we're not going to be able to complete the cross-examination of this witness today, so having regard to the number of procedural matters to which we must return, we think this would be a convenient point to excuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour. But if you don't mind, I would like to finish with this document, and I will probably need a minute or two only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to paragraph 104 of this law, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we just -- I'm so sorry. Could we just identify that this is the old law, not the Republika Srpska law. This is the Bosnia-Herzegovina, pre-the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Counsel, perhaps we should pick this up on Monday. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. We'll continue on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I have an explanation and a caution for you. The explanation is that it is regretted that you're going to be inconvenienced by having to remain in The Hague over the weekend. As you would have heard me indicate to counsel, it is simply impossible to complete your cross-examination in the time available this afternoon, so it is regrettable that you will have to remain here over the weekend to return on Monday. The caution is this: You are now in the witness box, sworn as a witness, and therefore you cannot have contact with counsel on either side until you are released by the Court. Furthermore, in your conversation with anybody other than counsel, you can't discuss your testimony in this matter. Do you understand what I have said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So the witness may now be excused until Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: First of all, on the matter of the videolink, the motion for this one witness is granted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Then there is another matter. On the 25th of September, the Prosecution filed a motion seeking to amend its exhibit list to add three photographic presentation of crime sites. Neither Defence has yet responded to this motion. The photographic presentation which relates to the municipality of Kotor Varos was created in August 29. The two other presentations are currently being created by the Prosecution, the Trail Chamber considers that the Prosecution has acted diligently in producing this presentation and that it's in the interest of justice that the Prosecution's exhibit list be amended to include them. And issues as to admissibility will be addressed at the time the document is tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the last matter is the two witnesses who are coming -- who are scheduled to come on Monday of next week. We applied way back in, I think, February to have them as 92 ter. Can we -- February of last year. Can we have a decision on those two witnesses, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I overheard that, I'm afraid, but -- but, Your Honour, I think something formally needs to be said. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. And this is what we'll say. Look at the clock, it's already over our time. We have to stop in order to protect the interests of the interpreters, so we will rule on this, this afternoon, and you'll be told the results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment to Monday afternoon in this courtroom. I trust everyone has a safe weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of October, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
